newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Austereo to match 95/96 result this yr.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Austereo to match 95/96 result this yr.

text.p: Radio station operator Austereo Ltd said on Tuesday it was reasonably confident at this stage that the 1996/97 financial year would be at least as successful as the previous financial year.
"We are budgeting for an increase in profit this year but we are only four months into the year," chairman John Kirby told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
"We cannot predict with certainty what is going to eventuate over the next eight months," he said.
"We are are reasonably confident at this stage we will have a year at least as successful as last year," he said.
Kirby earlier said the company was currently behind budget targets for 1996/97 but was on par with last year's results.
He said September capital cities radio revenue was some 11 percent behind last year, but October and November had shown earlie signs of industry growth.
Kirby said revenues were currently down on budget because Austereo had anticipated a growth which had not eventuated.

"Nevertheless we are very strong in the market...We have been able to hold the line so, while we don't have an increase that we budget for, we certainly don't have the 11 percent decrease everyone else is wearing," he said.
"We expect an increase in revenue and we expect a continuing benefit from synergy savings," he said.
Kirby said Austereo, which was beaten this year in its bid for Queensland radio broadcaster SEA FM, still was looking at further acquisition opportunities in Australia.

However, managing director Peter Harvie said Austereo would not be able, under current broadcasting regulations, to pursue the strategic Hot Hits One FM station in western Sydney which, according to market speculation, could be up for sale.

Kirby said the Austereo-MCM International radio programming joint venture was planning to expand into television production in Australia and Britain, looking primarily as breakfast, game and music productions rather than drama.
However, Austereo did not have the financial capacity nor interest to seek entry to a television station or network.

Kirby, who is also a key executive of entertainment and leisure group Village Roadshow Ltd which holds a 52.8 percent stake in Austereo, said any move to lift Village's stake was "not on the agenda at the moment".
